conclusions: As N → ∞, ZN converges in distribution to N(0,1).
The CDF of ZN converges pointwise to the CDF of the standard normal distribution.

definitions_and_conventions: Under the stated i.i.d. mean/variance context, ZN = (1/(σ sqrt(N))) sum_{i=1}^N (Xi − μ).
The standard normal distribution N(0,1) has density f(x) = (1/sqrt(2π))e^(−x²/2) for x ∈ R.
The source explains convergence in distribution here using CDF convergence and then an upper-tail formulation.

contract_plain_english: For an i.i.d. sequence with common mean μ and variance σ², form SN from the first N variables and normalize it as ZN = (SN − E SN)/sqrt(Var(SN)) = (1/(σ sqrt(N))) sum_{i=1}^N (Xi − μ). As N tends to infinity, ZN approaches the standard normal law. The source explains this by saying that the normalized sum's CDF converges pointwise to the standard-normal CDF and, equivalently in this setting, that for every real t its upper-tail probability P{ZN ≥ t} converges to the standard-normal upper tail. The printed sentence contains no continuity-point qualifier; the all-t statement is appropriate because the standard-normal CDF is continuous everywhere.
